name: Space station (ISS)

gravity.note: NASA HRP gravity page: research on the space station helps manage the health effects of microgravity.

radiation_rate.note: NASA LSAH Newsletter, Oct 2023, Vol 28 Issue 2, p. 6: ISS astronauts receive doses in the order of 0.5 mSv/day. Order of magnitude; it varies with solar activity and shielding.

comm_delay.note: NASA: the relay through the Space Network happens in milliseconds, so there is no noticeable delay. Shown as 0 min to compare with the Mars profile.

evacuation.value: return to Earth within 24 hours of deciding to return early
evacuation.note: NASA CCT-REQ-1130 Rev E-1 (ISS Crew Transportation and Services Requirements, 2016), p. 6: the crew will return to Earth within 24 hours of a declaration of an intention to return early, for example for a medical event. A requirement on the crew vehicle, not a promise for every case.

medical_kit.note: No public kit list was read for this profile. Contents are not listed so no drug name appears in content.

exercise_kit.note: Devices NASA JSC lists for the ISS.

crew_size.note: NASA: an international crew of seven people live and work on the station.

duration.note: NASA Crew-8: a six-month mission. Some crew stay about a year.

dust.note: Planetary dust is a surface hazard; no source read states the station value.

closed_habitat.note: NASA HRP hazards: isolation and confinement, and hostile closed environments inside a spacecraft.

delay_label: near real time from low Earth orbit (sourced: comm_delay)
spec4_note: Spec 4 fields. crew: Spec 1 replay crew ids (team value). equipment: every item the CPR and chest-pain protocols use. A defibrillator is part of the crew health care system (CHeCS) on the ISS (Hinkelbein et al. 2020, rationale for Recommendation 10); the other items are assumed on board (team value).
